`src/d3d/render_thread.cpp`:

```cpp
// The Vulkan backend on a thread of its own. The title's render thread records each call with what the console
// takes at call time (state changes, resource headers, indices, rects) and goes on; vertex, texture and surface memory
// are read when the draw runs, as the console's GPU reads them after the call returns. The XDK's fences, busy checks
// and locks wait for that.
#include <arm_neon.h>
#include <pthread.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstring>
#include <deque>
#include <mutex>
#include <thread>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <vector>

#include "core/diag.h"
#include "core/log.h"
#include "d3d/gpu_frame.h"
#include "gpu/backend.h"
#include "kernel/kernel.h"
#include "kernel/memory.h"

namespace gpu {

namespace {

// commands handed over at once, so the render thread keeps close behind and a wait is short
constexpr uint32_t kBatchCommands = 64;

// resource headers the render thread reads: common, data, lock, format, size
constexpr uint32_t kHeaderBytes = 20;
constexpr uint32_t kHeaderSlot = 32;
constexpr uint32_t kHeaderRing = 1u << 20;  // guest memory for header copies; a copy is renewed after half a ring

enum class WaitFor : uint8_t { ReadBack, Resource, Fence, Flush, Copy, Frame, Count };

enum class Op : uint8_t { State, Draw, Clear, Copy, Present, Sync, RecordLate, Flush, Gamma, ClearReport, GetReport };

struct Cmd {
    Op op;
    uint32_t a = 0;
    uint32_t b = 0;
    uint32_t c = 0;
    uint32_t d = 0;
    float f = 0;
    // data and size: bytes in Batch::bytes
    uint32_t data = 0;
    uint32_t size = 0;
    // index in Batch::vs / ps: the shader changed
    int32_t vs = -1;
    int32_t ps = -1;
    Surface s1;
    Surface s2;
};

struct Batch {
    uint64_t id = 0;
    std::vector<Cmd> cmds;
    std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<VertexShader>> vs;
    std::vector<std::shared_ptr<PixelShader>> ps;
};

// the plain data in State, around its shader pointers and the resource headers (sent as copies); of the transforms only
// view, projection, texture and world are drawn with, of the simple render states only those native/vulkan.cpp and
// MakePixelKey read: alpha test to depth offset, the combiners with their constants and the final combiner
struct Range {
    size_t off;
    size_t len;
};
size_t At(const State& s, const void* p) {
    return size_t(static_cast<const uint8_t*>(p) - reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(&s));
}
// bytes of the simple render states from method first to method last
size_t SimpleBytes(uint32_t first, uint32_t last) { return size_t(last - first) + sizeof(uint32_t); }
std::vector<Range> StateRanges() {
    static const State s;
    return {
        {At(s, &s.simple[kMAlphaTestEnable >> 2]), SimpleBytes(kMAlphaTestEnable, kMDepthOffset)},
        // the combiners themselves too: a title's pixel shader render states change them after SetPixelShader
        {At(s, &s.simple[kMPsAlphaInputs >> 2]), SimpleBytes(kMPsAlphaInputs, kMPsFinalEfgh)},
        {At(s, &s.simple[kMPsConstant0 >> 2]), SimpleBytes(kMPsConstant0, kMPsRgbInputs + 7 * 4)},
        {At(s, &s.simple[kMPsCompareMode >> 2]), SimpleBytes(kMPsCompareMode, kMPsCompareMode)},
        {At(s, &s.simple[kMPsFinalConstant0 >> 2]), SimpleBytes(kMPsFinalConstant0, kMPsFinalConstant1)},
        {At(s, &s.simple[kMPsRgbOutputs >> 2]), SimpleBytes(kMPsRgbOutputs, kMPsInputTexture)},
        {At(s, &s.rs), At(s, &s.textures) - At(s, &s.rs)},
        {At(s, &s.index_buffer), At(s, &s.vs) - At(s, &s.index_buffer)},
        {At(s, &s.vsc), At(s, &s.rt) - At(s, &s.vsc)},
        {At(s, &s.scissor_count), At(s, &s.transforms) - At(s, &s.scissor_count)},
        {At(s, &s.transforms[2]), 2 * sizeof(s.transforms[0])},
        {At(s, &s.transforms[16]), 4 * sizeof(s.transforms[0])},
        {At(s, &s.transforms[256]), sizeof(s.transforms[0])},
        {At(s, &s.material), sizeof(State) - At(s, &s.material)},
    };
}

// equal bytes, 16 at a time: most of the state is compared on every draw
bool Same(const uint8_t* a, const uint8_t* b, size_t n) {
    size_t i = 0;
    uint8x16_t diff = vdupq_n_u8(0);
    for (; i + 16 <= n; i += 16) diff = vorrq_u8(diff, veorq_u8(vld1q_u8(a + i), vld1q_u8(b + i)));
    if (vmaxvq_u8(diff)) return false;
    return i == n || !std::memcmp(a + i, b + i, n - i);
}

constexpr size_t kPiece = 64;  // bytes compared and sent at once

// equal 64 byte pieces, the scan over the state on every draw
bool SamePiece(const uint8_t* a, const uint8_t* b) {
    uint8x16_t diff = vdupq_n_u8(0);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < kPiece; i += 16) diff = vorrq_u8(diff, veorq_u8(vld1q_u8(a + i), vld1q_u8(b + i)));
    return vmaxvq_u8(diff) == 0;
}

using Clock = std::chrono::steady_clock;
uint64_t Ns(Clock::time_point t) {
    return uint64_t(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(Clock::now() - t).count());
}
// the perf diagnostic's clock, read on every call only when it is on
Clock::time_point PerfNow() { return diag::Perf() ? Clock::now() : Clock::time_point{}; }
void AddCapture(Clock::time_point t) {
    if (diag::Perf()) g_perf_capture_ns += Ns(t);
}

class Threaded final : public Backend {
public:
    explicit Threaded(std::unique_ptr<Backend> inner) : inner_(std::move(inner)), ranges_(StateRanges()) {
        g_vsc_counted = true;
        ring_ = mem::AllocSystem(kHeaderRing, 64);
        cur_ = NewBatch();
        std::thread([this] { Run(); }).detach();
    }
    ~Threaded() override {
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(m_);
            stop_ = true;
        }
        cv_.notify_all();
        std::unique_lock lock(m_);
        // at exit the worker may be gone mid-batch: then the inner backend is left, not freed under it
        if (!done_cv_.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::milliseconds(500), [&] { return exited_; })) (void)inner_.release();
    }

    bool Init(uint32_t width, uint32_t height) override { return inner_->Init(width, height); }

    void Draw(const State& s, uint32_t prim, uint32_t start, uint32_t count, const uint8_t* indices) override {
        auto t = PerfNow();
        SendState(s);
        Cmd c{Op::Draw};
        c.a = prim;
        c.b = start;
        c.c = count;
        if (indices) {
            c.d = 1;
            c.data = Put(indices, size_t(count) * 2);
        }
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
        for (uint32_t tex : s.textures) Use(tex);
        for (uint32_t pal : s.palettes) Use(pal);
        for (const auto& st : s.streams) Use(st.vb);
        Use(s.rt.header);
        Use(s.zs.header);
        Written(s.rt);
        if (cur_->cmds.size() >= kBatchCommands) Submit();
        AddCapture(t);
    }

    void Clear(const State& s, uint32_t count, const uint8_t* rects, uint32_t flags, uint32_t color, float z,
               uint32_t stencil) override {
        auto t = PerfNow();
        SendState(s);
        Cmd c{Op::Clear};
        c.a = count;
        c.b = flags;
        c.c = color;
        c.d = stencil;
        c.f = z;
        if (count && rects) {
            c.data = Put(rects, size_t(count) * 16);
            c.size = count * 16;
        }
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
        Use(s.rt.header);
        Use(s.zs.header);
        if (flags & kClearTarget) Written(s.rt);
        AddCapture(t);
    }

    // rects and points are taken now; the copy itself, CPU or GPU, runs in order like the console's
    void Copy(const Surface& src, const Surface& dst, uint32_t count, uint32_t src_rects,
              uint32_t dst_points) override {
        auto t = PerfNow();
        Cmd c{Op::Copy};
        c.a = count;
        c.b = count && src_rects ? Scratch(kernel::HostPtr(src_rects), count * 16) : 0;
        c.c = count && dst_points ? Scratch(kernel::HostPtr(dst_points), count * 8) : 0;
        c.s1 = src;
        c.s1.header = Header(src.header);
        c.s2 = dst;
        c.s2.header = Header(dst.header);
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
        Use(src.header);
        Use(dst.header);
        Written(dst);
        AddCapture(t);
    }

    void Present(const Surface& front) override {
        auto t = PerfNow();
        Cmd c{Op::Present};
        c.s1 = front;
        c.s1.header = Header(front.header);
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
        Use(front.header);
        uint64_t id = Submit();
        AddCapture(t);
        // the title records one frame while the one before it draws
        Wait(last_present_, WaitFor::Frame, nullptr);
        last_present_ = id;
    }

    void Sync(uint32_t data, uint32_t) override { ReadBack(data, false); }

    void SyncLate(uint32_t data) override {
        if (!inner_->DeliverLate(data)) {
            if (diag::Perf()) {
                LOG_FIRST(16, "render thread: no finished copy of %08X for a NOOVERWRITE lock, reading it back now", data);
            }
            written_.insert(data);
            ReadBack(data, true);
        }
        Cmd c{Op::RecordLate};
        c.a = data;
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
    }

    void Flush() override {
        cur_->cmds.push_back(Cmd{Op::Flush});
        Wait(Submit(), WaitFor::Flush, "flush");
    }

    void SetGamma(const uint8_t* ramp) override {
        Cmd c{Op::Gamma};
        c.data = Put(ramp, 768);
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
    }

    void ClearReport() override { cur_->cmds.push_back(Cmd{Op::ClearReport}); }
    void GetReport(uint32_t report) override {
        Cmd c{Op::GetReport};
        c.a = report;
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
    }

    uint32_t Fence() override { return uint32_t(cur_->id); }
    bool FencePending(uint32_t fence) override { return fence > done_.load(); }
    void WaitFence(uint32_t fence) override { Wait(fence, WaitFor::Fence, "fence"); }
    bool Busy(uint32_t resource) override {
        auto it = last_use_.find(resource);
        return it != last_use_.end() && it->second > done_.load();
    }
    void WaitResource(uint32_t resource) override {
        auto it = last_use_.find(resource);
        if (it != last_use_.end()) Wait(it->second, WaitFor::Resource, "resource");
    }

private:
    Batch* NewBatch() {
        Batch* b;
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(m_);
            if (free_.empty()) {
                b = new Batch;
            } else {
                b = free_.back();
                free_.pop_back();
            }
        }
        b->id = ++next_id_;
        return b;
    }

    uint32_t Put(const void* p, size_t n) {
        size_t at = (cur_->bytes.size() + 3) & ~size_t(3);
        cur_->bytes.resize(at + n);
        std::memcpy(cur_->bytes.data() + at, p, n);
        return uint32_t(at);
    }

    void ReadBack(uint32_t data, bool late) {
        // only surfaces the GPU wrote since the last read-back hold anything newer than guest memory
        if (!written_.erase(data)) return;
        (late ? g_perf_sync_late : g_perf_sync_block)++;
        if (diag::Perf() && logged_.insert(uint64_t(data) << 1 | (late ? 1 : 0)).second) {
            const char* why = late ? "a NOOVERWRITE lock without a finished copy" : "a lock / BlockOnResource";
            LOGI("render thread: read-back of %08X for %s", data, why);
        }
        Cmd c{Op::Sync};
        c.a = data;
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
        Wait(Submit(), WaitFor::ReadBack, "read-back");
    }

    // bytes the render thread reads through a guest address, in the header ring
    uint32_t Scratch(const void* p, uint32_t n) {
        uint32_t size = (n + kHeaderSlot - 1) & ~(kHeaderSlot - 1);
        if (ring_pos_ % kHeaderRing + size > kHeaderRing) ring_pos_ += kHeaderRing - ring_pos_ % kHeaderRing;
        uint32_t at = ring_ + uint32_t(ring_pos_ % kHeaderRing);
        ring_pos_ += size;
        std::memcpy(kernel::HostPtr(at), p, n);
        return at;
    }

    // A header as it is now. The console's push buffer takes a texture's format and address, and a surface's or vertex
    // buffer's address, when they are set; the title points the same header elsewhere before the GPU gets there.
    uint32_t Header(uint32_t header) {
        if (!header || !ring_) return header;
        // vertex buffer, index buffer and palette headers are 12 bytes: reading 20 can run off the end of the heap
        const uint32_t type = kernel::R32(header) & 0x70000;  // 0 vertex, 0x10000 index, 0x30000 palette
        uint8_t now[kHeaderBytes] = {};
        std::memcpy(now, kernel::HostPtr(header), type < 0x20000 || type == 0x30000 ? 12 : kHeaderBytes);
        Recent<HeaderCopy>& r = recent_headers_[(header >> 3) & 63];
        HeaderCopy& c = r.key == header ? *r.value : headers_[header];
        r = {header, &c};
        if (c.made && !std::memcmp(c.bytes, now, kHeaderBytes) && ring_pos_ - c.made < kHeaderRing / 2) return c.at;
        c.at = Scratch(now, kHeaderBytes);
        c.made = ring_pos_;
        std::memcpy(c.bytes, now, kHeaderBytes);
        return c.at;
    }

    // a field of the render thread's State, when it differs from what was sent
    void Delta(const void* field, const void* value, size_t n) {
        uint8_t* sent = reinterpret_cast<uint8_t*>(&sent_) + At(sent_, field);
        if (Same(sent, static_cast<const uint8_t*>(value), n)) return;
        std::memcpy(sent, value, n);
        uint32_t head[2] = {uint32_t(At(sent_, field)), uint32_t(n)};
        size_t at = cur_->bytes.size();
        cur_->bytes.resize(at + 8 + n);
        std::memcpy(cur_->bytes.data() + at, head, 8);
        std::memcpy(cur_->bytes.data() + at + 8, value, n);
    }

    // the pieces of a range that changed, the last one shorter when the range ends inside it
    void SendRange(const uint8_t* now, const Range& r) {
        const uint8_t* sent = reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(&sent_);
        size_t off = r.off;
        size_t end = r.off + r.len;
        for (; off + kPiece <= end; off += kPiece) {
            if (!SamePiece(sent + off, now + off)) Delta(sent + off, now + off, kPiece);
        }
        if (off < end) Delta(sent + off, now + off, end - off);
    }

    // what changed since the last command, in 64 byte pieces
    void SendState(const State& s) {
        const uint8_t* now = reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(&s);
        Cmd c{Op::State};
        size_t first = cur_->bytes.size();
        for (const Range& r : ranges_) SendRange(now, r);
        std::array<uint32_t, 4> textures;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) textures[i] = Header(s.textures[i]);
        Delta(&sent_.textures, &textures, sizeof(textures));
        std::array<uint32_t, 4> palettes;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 4; i++) palettes[i] = Header(s.palettes[i]);
        Delta(&sent_.palettes, &palettes, sizeof(palettes));
        auto streams = s.streams;
        for (auto& st : streams) st.vb = Header(st.vb);
        Delta(&sent_.streams, &streams, sizeof(streams));
        Surface rt = s.rt;
        Surface zs = s.zs;
        rt.header = Header(rt.header);
        zs.header = Header(zs.header);
        Delta(&sent_.rt, &rt, sizeof(rt));
        Delta(&sent_.zs, &zs, sizeof(zs));
        if (s.vs.get() != sent_.vs.get()) {
            sent_.vs = s.vs;
            c.vs = int32_t(cur_->vs.size());
            cur_->vs.push_back(s.vs);
        }
        if (s.ps.get() != sent_.ps.get()) {
            sent_.ps = s.ps;
            c.ps = int32_t(cur_->ps.size());
            cur_->ps.push_back(s.ps);
        }
        if (cur_->bytes.size() == first && c.vs < 0 && c.ps < 0) return;
        c.data = uint32_t(first);
        c.size = uint32_t(cur_->bytes.size() - first);
        cur_->cmds.push_back(c);
    }

    // resources by guest header: the batch that last read them
    void Use(uint32_t header) {
        if (!header) return;
        Recent<uint64_t>& r = recent_uses_[(header >> 3) & 63];
        if (r.key != header) r = {header, &last_use_[header]};
        *r.value = cur_->id;
    }
    void Written(const Surface& s) {
        if (s.header) written_.insert(mem::VirtualFromPhysical(s.data));
    }

    uint64_t Submit() {
        uint64_t id = cur_->id;
        bool wake;
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(m_);
            queue_.push_back(cur_);
            wake = idle_;
        }
        // a notify is a futex call on Android, waiter or not: only when the render thread sleeps
        if (wake) cv_.notify_one();
        cur_ = NewBatch();
        return id;
    }

    void Wait(uint64_t id, WaitFor kind, const char* why) {
        if (!id || done_.load() >= id) return;
        if (id >= cur_->id) id = Submit();
        auto t = Clock::now();
        {
            std::unique_lock lock(m_);
            waiting_++;
            done_cv_.wait(lock, [&] { return done_.load() >= id; });
            waiting_--;
        }
        uint64_t ns = Ns(t);
        g_perf_wait_ns += ns;
        g_perf_wait_kind_ns[size_t(kind)] += ns;
        if (why) {
            g_perf_waits++;
            if (diag::Perf()) LOG_FIRST(32, "render thread: the title waited %.2f ms for a %s", ns / 1e6, why);
        }
    }

    void Run() {
        pthread_setname_np(pthread_self(), "render");
        for (;;) {
            Batch* b;
            {
                std::unique_lock lock(m_);
                idle_ = true;
                cv_.wait(lock, [&] { return stop_ || !queue_.empty(); });
                idle_ = false;
                if (queue_.empty()) break;
                b = queue_.front();
                queue_.pop_front();
            }
            auto t = PerfNow();
            for (const Cmd& c : b->cmds) Execute(*b, c);
            if (diag::Perf()) g_perf.render_ns += Ns(t);
            uint64_t id = b->id;
            b->cmds.clear();
            b->bytes.clear();
            b->vs.clear();
            b->ps.clear();
            bool wake;
            {
                std::lock_guard lock(m_);
                free_.push_back(b);
                done_.store(id);
                wake = waiting_ > 0;
            }
            if (wake) done_cv_.notify_all();
        }
        std::lock_guard lock(m_);
        exited_ = true;
        done_cv_.notify_all();
    }

    void Execute(const Batch& b, const Cmd& c) {
        const uint8_t* data = b.bytes.data() + c.data;
        switch (c.op) {
            case Op::State: {
                uint8_t* s = reinterpret_cast<uint8_t*>(&state_);
                static const size_t vsc_begin = At(state_, &state_.vsc), vsc_end = vsc_begin + sizeof(state_.vsc);
                for (const uint8_t* p = data; p < data + c.size;) {
                    uint32_t head[2];
                    std::memcpy(head, p, 8);
                    std::memcpy(s + head[0], p + 8, head[1]);
                    if (head[0] < vsc_end && head[0] + head[1] > vsc_begin) g_vsc_changes++;
                    p += 8 + head[1];
                }
                if (c.vs >= 0) state_.vs = b.vs[size_t(c.vs)];
                if (c.ps >= 0) state_.ps = b.ps[size_t(c.ps)];
                break;
            }
            case Op::Draw: inner_->Draw(state_, c.a, c.b, c.c, c.d ? data : nullptr); break;
            case Op::Clear: inner_->Clear(state_, c.a, c.size ? data : nullptr, c.b, c.c, c.f, c.d); break;
            case Op::Copy: inner_->Copy(c.s1, c.s2, c.a, c.b, c.c); break;
            case Op::Present: inner_->Present(c.s1); break;
            case Op::Sync: inner_->Sync(c.a, 0); break;
            case Op::RecordLate: inner_->RecordLate(c.a); break;
            case Op::Flush: inner_->Flush(); break;
            case Op::Gamma: inner_->SetGamma(data); break;
            case Op::ClearReport: inner_->ClearReport(); break;
            case Op::GetReport: inner_->GetReport(c.a); break;
        }
    }

    std::unique_ptr<Backend> inner_;
    std::vector<Range> ranges_;

    // the title's thread
    struct HeaderCopy {
        uint32_t at = 0;
        uint64_t made = 0;  // ring_pos_ after it was written
        uint8_t bytes[kHeaderBytes];
    };
    std::unordered_map<uint32_t, HeaderCopy> headers_;
    // the last few lookups, in front of the maps (their elements stay put)
    template <typename T>
    struct Recent {
        uint32_t key = 0;
        T* value = nullptr;
    };
    std::array<Recent<HeaderCopy>, 64> recent_headers_{};
    std::array<Recent<uint64_t>, 64> recent_uses_{};
    uint32_t ring_ = 0;
    uint64_t ring_pos_ = 0;
    Batch* cur_ = nullptr;
    State sent_;  // the state as the render thread will have it
    std::unordered_map<uint32_t, uint64_t> last_use_;
    std::unordered_set<uint32_t> written_;  // surfaces drawn since their last read-back, by data address
    std::unordered_set<uint64_t> logged_;   // perf diagnostic: read-backs named once, by address and kind
    uint64_t next_id_ = 0;
    uint64_t last_present_ = 0;

    // the render thread
    State state_;

    std::mutex m_;
    std::condition_variable cv_;
    std::condition_variable done_cv_;
    std::deque<Batch*> queue_;
    std::vector<Batch*> free_;
    std::atomic<uint64_t> done_{0};
    bool stop_ = false;
    bool exited_ = false;
    bool idle_ = false;  // the render thread waits for a batch
    int waiting_ = 0;    // title threads waiting for a batch to be done
};

}  // namespace

std::unique_ptr<Backend> CreateThreadedBackend(std::unique_ptr<Backend> inner) {
    return std::make_unique<Threaded>(std::move(inner));
}

}  // namespace gpu
```

`src/game/fe_mouse.cpp`:

```cpp
// Most Wanted's menus are FEng packages, and FEng kept the PC's mouse: packages carry mouse regions (FF_MouseObject,
// MainMenu.fng's five: its arrows, its middle icon and the button prompts) that it tests a pointer against and sends
// over, press and click messages for (FEngine::UpdateMouseState, 0x158500). The console's FEngine has its mouse off
// (bMouseActive, FEngine + 1) and its interface's GetMouseInfo is an empty function shared with other empty methods
// (0x19BC0), so the touch screen is the mouse here: the interface's vtable slot points at a host function instead,
// and the mouse is on while a package that takes input has regions and a finger is on it or just left it: else the
// front end runs as the console's, its mouse off.
// The console's screens left the PC's mouse handling out (ArrayScroller::UpdateMouse is empty); what the packages'
// own scripts do with a click still works (MainMenu's arrows, a dialog's OK). A tap on the highlighted button, which
// those screens accept on the pad's A alone, is told to the touch controls to press A (FeTakeAccept).
#include <atomic>
#include <cctype>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "common/aspect.h"
#include "common/fe_mouse.h"
#include "common/options.h"
#include "cpu/x86_context.h"
#include "kernel/kernel.h"
#include "kernel/memory.h"

namespace dispatch {
uint32_t HostThunk(X86Func* fn);  // sdk/runtime/cpu/dispatch.cpp
}

namespace game {

void OptionsMenuTick(X86Context& ctx);  // options_menu.cpp

namespace {

// cFEng's instance; its first field the FEngine
constexpr uint32_t kFEng = 0x48E94C;
// FEngine: bMouseActive, the first package, the game's interface
constexpr uint32_t kMouseActive = 0x1, kFirstPackage = 0xE0, kInterface = 0x108;
constexpr uint32_t kGetMouseInfoSlot = 0x44;  // FEGameInterface's vtable
// FEPackage: the next, its controllers, input taken, its current button, its mouse regions
constexpr uint32_t kNext = 0x4, kControlMask = 0x20, kInputEnabled = 0x28, kCurrentButton = 0x8C, kMouseObjects = 0xB0;
constexpr int kMaxPackages = 64;
// FEngTestForIntersection(float x, float y, FEObject*), cdecl: a point of FEng's screen on an object as drawn
constexpr uint32_t kTestForIntersection = 0x10CF20;

std::atomic<bool> g_menu{false};
std::atomic<uint32_t> g_package{0};  // the menu's package, game thread
// the finger, FEng's screen; each touch counts a press, so one shorter than a frame is still seen down
std::atomic<int32_t> g_x{0}, g_y{0};
std::atomic<bool> g_down{false};
bool g_reported_down = false;  // the button as GetMouseInfo gave it this update, game thread
std::atomic<uint32_t> g_presses{0};
// presents the mouse stays on after a touch: past the pointer's leaving, so its regions see it go
constexpr int kMouseFrames = 30;
std::atomic<int> g_mouse_frames{0};
// the press came down on this package's highlighted button
std::atomic<uint32_t> g_accept_package{0}, g_accept_button{0};
// the menu has no mouse regions and prompts A (a tutorial's "Press A To Continue"): a tap anywhere is its A
std::atomic<bool> g_tap_anywhere{false};
constexpr uint32_t kAnywhere = 1;  // g_accept_button for such a tap

uint32_t FEngine() {
    uint32_t feng = kernel::R32(kFEng);
    return feng ? kernel::R32(feng) : 0;
}

uint32_t Bits(float f) {
    uint32_t b;
    std::memcpy(&b, &f, 4);
    return b;
}

// the press came down on the package's highlighted button, one FEng's mouse does not click itself (a dialog's OK is
// a mouse region: A as well would accept the next screen too)
constexpr uint32_t kObjectFlags = 0x1C, kMouseObject = 1u << 17;
bool OnCurrentButton(X86Context& ctx) {
    uint32_t p = g_package, button = p ? kernel::R32(p + kCurrentButton) : 0;
    if (!button || (kernel::R32(button + kObjectFlags) & kMouseObject)) return false;
    uint32_t saved[] = {ctx.eax, ctx.ecx, ctx.edx, ctx.ebx, ctx.esi, ctx.edi, ctx.ebp};
    uint32_t hit = kernel::CallGuest(ctx, kTestForIntersection, {Bits(float(g_x)), Bits(float(g_y)), button}) & 0xFF;
    ctx.eax = saved[0], ctx.ecx = saved[1], ctx.edx = saved[2], ctx.ebx = saved[3], ctx.esi = saved[4];
    ctx.edi = saved[5], ctx.ebp = saved[6];
    return hit != 0;
}

bool KeyboardPackage(uint32_t p);
uint32_t PickKey(X86Context& ctx, uint32_t p);

// FEngine::Update's GetMouseInfo(FEMouseInfo&), thiscall: x, y, wheel and the buttons, int16 each. A press shows down
// for two updates at least, for the press and then the click on its release; then the pointer stays a few updates
// and leaves, so a resting pointer neither keeps an item hovered nor fights the pad
void GetMouseInfo(X86Context& ctx, uint8_t*) {
    constexpr int kHoldUpdates = 2, kStayUpdates = 4;
    constexpr int16_t kAway = -2000;
    static uint32_t seen = 0;
    static int hold = 0, stay = 0;
    uint32_t info = kernel::Args{ctx}[0];
    uint32_t presses = g_presses;
    if (presses != seen) {
        seen = presses;
        hold = kHoldUpdates;
        uint32_t p = g_package;
        if (!g_tap_anywhere) {  // FeTouch took that one
            if (p && KeyboardPackage(p)) g_accept_button = PickKey(ctx, p);
            else g_accept_button = OnCurrentButton(ctx) ? kernel::R32(p + kCurrentButton) : 0;
            g_accept_package = p;
        }
    }
    bool down = g_down || hold > 0;
    g_reported_down = down;
    if (hold > 0) hold--;
    if (down) stay = kStayUpdates;
    else if (stay > 0) stay--;
    bool here = down || stay > 0;
    kernel::W16(info, uint16_t(here ? int16_t(g_x.load()) : kAway));
    kernel::W16(info + 2, uint16_t(here ? int16_t(g_y.load()) : kAway));
    kernel::W16(info + 4, 0);
    kernel::W16(info + 6, down ? 1 : 0);  // FEMouse_Left
    OptionsMenuTick(ctx);
    kernel::Return(ctx, 0, 1);
}

// The menu's button prompts (the bar of "A Accept", "B Back", "Y Defaults"): in its package an image with the pad
// button's icon and the string after it in its group, the label; hidden ones, or ones in a hidden group, are not up
constexpr uint32_t kPackageObjects = 0x4C;
constexpr uint32_t kObjectNext = 0x4, kObjectType = 0x18, kObjectHidden = 1, kImageTexture = 0x24, kStringText = 0x64;
constexpr uint32_t kGroupCount = 0x60, kGroupObjects = 0x64;
constexpr uint32_t kTypeImage = 1, kTypeString = 2, kTypeGroup = 5;
// the prompts' textures, named for the PS2's buttons: A CROSS, B TRIANGLE, X SQUARE, Y CIRCLE, the triggers L1 and R1;
// the right stick RIGHT_ANALOG
constexpr uint32_t kPromptTextures[] = {0x02959349, 0x6851AAF5, 0x7A8B6BD0, 0x54A68051, 0x000005BC, 0x00000682};
constexpr uint32_t kRightStickTexture = 0xFBB0B78E;
constexpr int kMaxObjects = 600;
constexpr uint32_t kPackageName = 0xC;
uint32_t Peek(uint32_t va);

// The game's keyboard (Keyboard.fng, a profile's name): a grid of 15 columns of buttons (flag kButtonObject), the
// letters' and digits' and under them the cells of Space, Lowercase, Backspace and Done; the dpad moves the package's
// current button and A presses it. A tap on a key makes it the current button (FEPackage::SetCurrentButton, thiscall,
// the object and whether to send the highlight messages), then is a tap on the highlighted button, accepted as A
constexpr uint32_t kButtonObject = 1u << 28;
constexpr uint32_t kSetCurrentButton = 0x15CB30;
constexpr int kMaxKeys = 2000;  // the package's objects, both of its pages

bool KeyboardPackage(uint32_t p) {
    uint32_t name = Peek(p + kPackageName);
    char head[8] = {};
    for (uint32_t i = 0; name && i < 8 && mem::IsCommitted(name + i); i++) head[i] = char(kernel::G<uint8_t>(name + i));
    return std::memcmp(head, "Keyboard", 8) == 0;
}

// The keys are in groups, which FEngTestForIntersection leaves out (it tests an object's own place, in its group's
// units): a key is tested as drawn, by its cached render object's (+0x58) transform in the front end's 640x480 (its
// size at +0x30 and +0x44, its middle at +0x60 and +0x64). That 640x480 is drawn into the middle 576x448 of FEng's
// screen (the screen transform, 0x0D4888: 576 / width across and 448 / 480 down), times the front end's scale at
// 0x427BFC (the profile's, 1 on the disc's defaults)
constexpr uint32_t kRenderObject = 0x58;
constexpr uint32_t kRenderWidth = 0x30, kRenderHeight = 0x44, kRenderX = 0x60, kRenderY = 0x64;
constexpr float kSafeAcross = 576.0f / 640.0f, kSafeDown = 448.0f / 480.0f;
constexpr uint32_t kFeScale = 0x427BFC;

float PeekFloat(uint32_t va) {
    uint32_t b = Peek(va);
    float f;
    std::memcpy(&f, &b, 4);
    return f;
}

// the shown button under a point of the front end's 640x480, 0 for none; a hidden group's are not shown
uint32_t KeyAt(float x, float y, uint32_t first, int count, int& budget) {
    for (uint32_t o = first; o && budget-- > 0 && count != 0; o = Peek(o + kObjectNext), count--) {
        uint32_t flags = Peek(o + kObjectFlags);
        if (flags & kObjectHidden) continue;
        if (Peek(o + kObjectType) == kTypeGroup) {
            if (uint32_t key = KeyAt(x, y, Peek(o + kGroupObjects), int(Peek(o + kGroupCount)), budget)) return key;
            continue;
        }
        uint32_t r = (flags & kButtonObject) ? Peek(o + kRenderObject) : 0;
        if (r && std::fabs(x - PeekFloat(r + kRenderX)) * 2 <= std::fabs(PeekFloat(r + kRenderWidth)) &&
            std::fabs(y - PeekFloat(r + kRenderY)) * 2 <= std::fabs(PeekFloat(r + kRenderHeight)))
            return o;
    }
    return 0;
}

// the key under the finger made the current button, 0 for none
uint32_t PickKey(X86Context& ctx, uint32_t p) {
    int budget = kMaxKeys;
    // FEng's screen to the front end's 640x480: 480 times the aspect wide with the widescreen flag, else the 640
    // stretched across the frame (FeTouch)
    float aspect = Aspect(), across = aspect >= 1.5f ? 1.0f : 480.0f * aspect / 640.0f;
    float scale = PeekFloat(kFeScale);
    if (!(scale > 0.1f && scale < 2.0f)) scale = 1.0f;
    float x = float(g_x) / (kSafeAcross * across * scale) + 320.0f, y = float(g_y) / (kSafeDown * scale) + 240.0f;
    uint32_t key = KeyAt(x, y, Peek(p + kPackageObjects), -1, budget);
    if (!key || key == kernel::R32(p + kCurrentButton)) return key;
    uint32_t ecx = ctx.ecx;
    ctx.ecx = p;
    kernel::CallGuest(ctx, kSetCurrentButton, {key, 1});
    ctx.ecx = ecx;
    return key;
}

uint32_t Peek(uint32_t va) { return va && mem::IsCommitted(va) && mem::IsCommitted(va + 3) ? kernel::R32(va) : 0; }

// FEng's text, 16 bit characters, in capitals
std::string Label(uint32_t text) {
    std::string out;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; text && i < 24 && mem::IsCommitted(text + i * 2 + 1); i++) {
        uint16_t c = kernel::G<uint16_t>(text + i * 2);
        if (!c) break;
        out += c < 128 ? char(std::toupper(c)) : '?';
    }
    return out;
}

void ScanPrompts(uint32_t first, int count, FePrompts& out, int& budget) {
    int pending = -1;  // an icon waiting for its label
    for (uint32_t o = first; o && budget-- > 0 && count != 0; o = Peek(o + kObjectNext), count--) {
        if (Peek(o + kObjectFlags) & kObjectHidden) continue;
        uint32_t type = Peek(o + kObjectType);
        if (type == kTypeGroup) {
            ScanPrompts(Peek(o + kGroupObjects), int(Peek(o + kGroupCount)), out, budget);
        } else if (type == kTypeImage) {
            uint32_t texture = Peek(o + kImageTexture);
            if (texture == kRightStickTexture) {
                out.right_stick = true;
                pending = -1;
            }
            for (int i = 0; i < kFePromptCount; i++)
                if (texture == kPromptTextures[i]) {
                    out.shown[i] = true;
                    pending = i;
                }
        } else if (type == kTypeString && pending >= 0) {
            if (out.label[pending].empty()) out.label[pending] = Label(Peek(o + kStringText));
            pending = -1;
        }
    }
}

std::mutex g_prompts_lock;
FePrompts g_prompts;  // the menu's, lately

}  // namespace

FePrompts CurrentFePrompts() {
    std::lock_guard lock(g_prompts_lock);
    return g_menu ? g_prompts : FePrompts{};
}

void FeFrame() {
    uint32_t fe = FEngine();
    if (!fe) {
        g_menu = false;
        return;
    }
    static const uint32_t thunk = dispatch::HostThunk(GetMouseInfo);
    if (uint32_t iface = kernel::R32(fe + kInterface)) {
        uint32_t slot = kernel::R32(iface) + kGetMouseInfoSlot;
        if (kernel::R32(slot) != thunk) kernel::W32(slot, thunk);
    }
    // a package taking input with mouse regions; else one with no regions showing a pad prompt (a tutorial's "Press A
    // To Continue"), which no tap reaches: a menu still, for the touch controls' ENTER and CLOSE, its mouse off. Not in
    // a race, where a HUD's prompt would take the pad away
    uint32_t menu = 0, prompted = 0;
    bool racing = Racing();
    FePrompts prompts, found;
    int n = 0;
    for (uint32_t p = kernel::R32(fe + kFirstPackage); p && n < kMaxPackages && !menu; p = kernel::R32(p + kNext), n++) {
        if (!kernel::G<uint8_t>(p + kInputEnabled) || !(kernel::R32(p + kControlMask) & 1)) continue;
        if (int32_t(kernel::R32(p + kMouseObjects)) > 0) {
            menu = p;
        } else if (!prompted && !racing) {
            int budget = kMaxObjects;
            ScanPrompts(Peek(p + kPackageObjects), -1, found, budget);
            if (found.shown[0] || found.shown[1] || found.shown[2] || found.shown[3]) prompted = p;
            else found = {};
        }
    }
    int frames = g_mouse_frames;
    if (g_down) frames = kMouseFrames;
    else if (frames > 0) frames--;
    g_mouse_frames = frames;
    // the keyboard has no mouse regions but its keys are tapped, through GetMouseInfo (PickKey)
    bool keyboard = !menu && prompted && KeyboardPackage(prompted);
    kernel::G<uint8_t>(fe + kMouseActive) = (menu != 0 || keyboard) && frames > 0;
    if (menu) {
        int budget = kMaxObjects;
        ScanPrompts(Peek(menu + kPackageObjects), -1, prompts, budget);
    } else if (prompted) {
        menu = prompted;
        prompts = found;
    }
    if (menu && KeyboardPackage(menu)) {
        for (int i = 2; i < kFePromptCount; i++) prompts.shown[i] = false;  // A and B stay, ENTER and CLOSE
        prompts.right_stick = false;
    }
    g_package = menu;
    g_menu = menu != 0;
    g_tap_anywhere = menu && menu == prompted && prompts.shown[0];
    std::lock_guard lock(g_prompts_lock);
    g_prompts = prompts;
}

bool FeMenuShown() { return g_menu; }
bool FeMouseDown() { return g_reported_down; }
bool FeFinger(float& x, float& y) {
    x = float(g_x), y = float(g_y);
    return g_down;
}

// FEng's mouse may have answered the tap itself (the splash's whole screen region, a dialog's OK): then the screen is
// on its way out and A as well would act on the one that follows (the splash's A landed on a loading screen and
// crashed it). The touch controls ask a moment after the tap; the same screen with the same item highlighted and
// still taking input gets its A
bool FeTakeAccept() {
    uint32_t p = g_accept_package.exchange(0), button = g_accept_button.exchange(0);
    if (!button || p != g_package || !g_menu || !kernel::G<uint8_t>(p + kInputEnabled)) return false;
    return button == kAnywhere || kernel::R32(p + kCurrentButton) == button;
}

bool FeTakeStart() { return false; }

// FEng's screen has its origin in the middle of the frame (MC_Main_GC.fng's OK, 39 under the middle) and is 480 high.
// Its hit tests (FEngTestForIntersection) take it as 480 times the frame's aspect wide, in square pixels: with the
// console's widescreen flag the front end lays out to that width (WidenAspect's), and without it (a frame under 3:2)
// its 640 wide layout is stretched to the frame and tested so. 640 there put a tap on a row's right arrow 11% short
// of it on a 3:2 tablet
void FeTouch(bool down, float u, float v) {
    float wide = 480.0f * Aspect();
    g_x = int32_t((u - 0.5f) * wide);
    g_y = int32_t((v - 0.5f) * 480.0f);
    if (down && !g_down) {
        g_presses++;
        if (g_tap_anywhere) {
            g_accept_package = g_package.load();
            g_accept_button = kAnywhere;
        }
    }
    g_down = down;
    g_mouse_frames = kMouseFrames;
}

}  // namespace game
```

```cpp
// Need for Speed: Most Wanted (Black Edition) needs no patch of its code to boot: the XDK it calls is all on the host.
// Its own hooks go here, [[hook]] entries in config/game.toml and X86_FUNC replacements of recompiled functions.
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>

#include "common/aspect.h"
#include "common/options.h"
#include "cpu/x86_ops.h"
#include "kernel/kernel.h"
#include "kernel/memory.h"

namespace game {

// The console's widescreen flag (XGetVideoFlags at boot, 0x0D0202, kept at 0x48099C; set from 3:2 on, native/main.cpp)
// gives the front end's and HUD's screen transform (0x0D4888, 0x0D8330: 576 / width across, 448 / 480 down) a frame
// 853 wide (480 * 16 / 9, at 0x427C00) for a 4:3 one's 640. It is the frame's own shape here, so 19.5:9 is not 16:9
// stretched
constexpr uint32_t kVideoFlags = 0x48099C, kWideWidth = 0x427C00;
void WidenAspect() {
    if (!(kernel::G<uint8_t>(kVideoFlags) & 1)) return;
    float w = 480.0f * Aspect();
    uint32_t bits;
    std::memcpy(&bits, &w, 4);
    kernel::W32(kWideWidth, bits);
}

// The 3D views' projection (0x0C7740, thiscall, the view's matrices in ecx, the eView first of 4 arguments): the
// camera's horizontal field of view ([[view + 0x40] + 0xC4], 16 bit angle) gives the x scale, cot of its half, at
// +0x40; the vertical is that angle times 9/16 with the widescreen flag (3/4 without), its scale at +0x54. A frame
// wider than 16:9 was the 16:9 picture stretched across it. The x scale is made the frame's, keeping the vertical
// (more of the road on the sides, not less above and below), before the view's matrix times it (0x2B91C4, at
// 0x0C7A04) gives the view projection that the frustum's planes are cut from, so what is culled widens with it.
// Only the views drawn over the frame: the players' (1, 2), their road reflections (4, 5) and glows (6, 7), the
// ones the game gives the widescreen angle; not the mirror's or the environment cube's faces
constexpr uint32_t kViewType = 0x4, kProjection = 0x40;
uint32_t g_widen_view = 0;  // the view's matrices while its projection is made, game thread
bool WideView(uint32_t type) { return type == 1 || type == 2 || (type >= 4 && type <= 7); }
}  // namespace game

X86_EXTERN_FUNC(__imp__sub_000C7740);
X86_FUNC(sub_000C7740) {
    uint32_t view = kernel::R32(ctx.esp + 4);
    bool wide = (kernel::G<uint8_t>(game::kVideoFlags) & 1) && view && game::WideView(kernel::R32(view + game::kViewType));
    game::g_widen_view = wide ? ctx.ecx : 0;
    __imp__sub_000C7740(ctx, base);
    game::g_widen_view = 0;
}

// the matrix product (out, a, b; cdecl): for the view being made, its projection is widened just before
X86_EXTERN_FUNC(__imp__sub_002B91C4);
X86_FUNC(sub_002B91C4) {
    uint32_t m = game::g_widen_view;
    if (m && kernel::R32(ctx.esp + 8) == m && kernel::R32(ctx.esp + 12) == m + game::kProjection) {
        game::g_widen_view = 0;
        float& x = kernel::G<float>(m + game::kProjection);
        x *= (16.0f / 9.0f) / game::Aspect();
    }
    __imp__sub_002B91C4(ctx, base);
}

namespace game {

// Switches the game reads and never writes, all 1 on the disc:
// - the cars' reflection is a cube drawn around the camera's car each frame, the world six times more (views 0x12 on,
//   0x0D7AD5), only while the byte at 0x4279D6 is set, one of a row of render switches at 0x4279CC. Off,
//   native/vulkan.cpp has the cars read a black cube, not the last one drawn
// - the particle system at 0x482CC0 (tyre smoke, sparks, crash debris) is drawn by 0x0CE8B0 (15 to 25 draws a frame)
//   only while the byte at 0x4279CF is set. Not its master switch, 0x434130: at 0 nothing spawns, and loading a race
//   with it off corrupted the heap (a crash in the allocator 0x054DC0 under 0x1C0D50), so the particles still run
// - a car's render (0x255490) draws the shadow under it, the CARSHADOW texture (0x24C0F0) and a second layer
//   (0x24BB90), only while the dword at 0x469910 is set
// - the wet road's reflection, the world drawn upside down into views 4 and 5 (0x0D787B), only while the dword at
//   0x427A3C is set. The road still samples view 4's target, [[view + 0x60] + 8] (0x0C0F90), so native/vulkan.cpp
//   gives it black when off, not the last one drawn
constexpr uint32_t kEnvMapSwitch = 0x4279D6, kParticleDrawSwitch = 0x4279CF, kCarShadowSwitch = 0x469910;
constexpr uint32_t kRoadReflectionSwitch = 0x427A3C, kRoadReflectionView = 0x48AE40;
constexpr uint32_t kEnvMapFace0Target = 0x48B4C0;  // view 0x12's [view + 0x60], the faces' views 0x70 apart

// the colour data of a view's target, [target + 8]'s, as a texture's address reads
uint32_t TargetData(uint32_t target) {
    uint32_t surface = target ? kernel::R32(target + 8) : 0;
    return surface ? mem::VirtualFromPhysical(kernel::R32(surface + 4)) : 0;
}
void ApplyGraphicsSwitches() {
    // HALF and QUARTER draw the cube every 2nd or 4th frame; between, the cars read the faces drawn last. OFF still
    // draws it every 512th: a cube never drawn leaves the paint white, whatever native/vulkan.cpp binds for it
    static uint32_t frame = 0;
    uint32_t rate = Opt().reflections;
    uint32_t every = rate < 3 ? 1u << rate : 512;
    bool envmap = frame++ % every == 0;
    kernel::G<uint8_t>(kEnvMapSwitch) = envmap ? 1 : 0;
    kernel::G<uint8_t>(kParticleDrawSwitch) = Opt().particles ? 1 : 0;
    kernel::W32(kCarShadowSwitch, Opt().shadows ? 1 : 0);
    kernel::W32(kRoadReflectionSwitch, Opt().road_reflections ? 1 : 0);
    g_road_reflection = TargetData(kernel::R32(kRoadReflectionView + 0x60));
    // the cube is its six faces' memory, the first face's at its start
    g_env_cube = TargetData(kernel::R32(kEnvMapFace0Target));
}

// Cheats:
// - the nitrous' drain (0x1E6A9A, an engine's NOS, [engine + 0xFC], less the flow) is 0 while the byte at 0x49A61C is
//   set, and the speedbreaker's (0x20E663, LocalPlayer +0x84 less the time) while the one at 0x4B9694 is: debug
//   switches the game reads there alone and never writes, 0 on the disc. Every car's nitrous, the racers' too
// - the career's cash is CareerSettings::CurrentCash, [[0x48EDD4] + 0x10] + 0xB4: the FEDatabase's first profile, as
//   the CASH_DATA string prints it (0x0F5425)
// - the cop manager ([0x494E40], ICopMgr at AICopManager +0x54) spawns no cop and starts no pursuit while its byte at
//   +0x60 is set (VehicleSpawningEnabled, 0x01A370): what the scripts' NoNewPursuitsOrCops sets (0x0130E0). The game
//   clears it again on a reset (0x01A9CD), so it is set at each present; off gives back the value it had
// - UnlockAllThings, the byte at 0x493D00 (SkipFE at 0x493C40 + 0xC0, as on the PC), is or'ed into every unlock test
//   (cars, parts, races: 0x12C0E0, 0x13B2DB, ...). The game sets it itself for a mode of its menus (0x1049FA), so off
//   gives back the value it had too
constexpr uint32_t kInfiniteNos = 0x49A61C, kInfiniteSpeedbreaker = 0x4B9694;
constexpr uint32_t kFeDatabase = 0x48EDD4, kProfileCash = 0xB4, kCheatCash = 9999999;
constexpr uint32_t kCopManager = 0x494E40, kNoNewCops = 0x60;
constexpr uint32_t kUnlockAllThings = 0x493D00;

// a game byte a cheat holds at 1 while on, given back as it was when it goes off or its object is made again
struct HeldByte {
    uint32_t held = 0;
    uint8_t before = 0;
    void Apply(bool on, uint32_t addr) {
        if (held && held != addr) held = 0;
        if (on && addr) {
            if (!held) {
                held = addr;
                before = kernel::G<uint8_t>(addr);
            }
            kernel::G<uint8_t>(addr) = 1;
        } else if (held) {
            kernel::G<uint8_t>(held) = before;
            held = 0;
        }
    }
};

void ApplyCheats() {
    const Options& o = Opt();
    kernel::G<uint8_t>(kInfiniteNos) = o.cheat_nos ? 1 : 0;
    kernel::G<uint8_t>(kInfiniteSpeedbreaker) = o.cheat_speedbreaker ? 1 : 0;
    if (o.cheat_cash) {
        uint32_t db = kernel::R32(kFeDatabase);
        uint32_t profile = db && mem::IsCommitted(db + 0x10) ? kernel::R32(db + 0x10) : 0;
        if (profile && mem::IsCommitted(profile + kProfileCash)) kernel::W32(profile + kProfileCash, kCheatCash);
    }
    static HeldByte no_cops, unlock_all;
    uint32_t mgr = kernel::R32(kCopManager);
    no_cops.Apply(o.cheat_no_police, mgr && mem::IsCommitted(mgr + kNoNewCops) ? mgr + kNoNewCops : 0);
    unlock_all.Apply(o.cheat_unlock_all, kUnlockAllThings);
}

// The movies' screens skip on A or START: FEAnyMovie (0x116230, the FE's and the story's), InGameAnyMovie (0x131A30)
// and the boot's (0x1311B0: EA logo, PSA, intro, attract; only while its byte at +0x2C allows). SKIP MOVIES has a tick
// (0xC98356BA, sent each frame, the subtitles' clock at 0x10D760) of each screen taken for A: once, as the skip posts
// the movie's end (0xC3960EB9) and a second would end what comes after; a few frames in, as the attract movie skipped
// on its first, with the boot screen's byte forced, hung on its first frame; and on the boot's screen only once its
// byte is set, the logos the game lets play out still play. A screen ends its movie once: a press of the player's
// after the skip (or before it) is taken for a tick, as a second end hung the attract movie on its frame. The screens'
// destructors forget them
constexpr uint32_t kMsgTick = 0xC98356BA, kMsgPadAccept = 0x406415E3, kMsgPadStart = 0xB5AF2461;
constexpr int kSkipTick = 10;
std::unordered_map<uint32_t, int> g_movie_ticks;  // a movie screen's ticks so far, past kSkipTick once skipped

// game thread, a movie screen's NotificationMessage (thiscall: the message, the object and two params)
void SkipMovie(X86Context& ctx, uint32_t allow_flag) {
    uint32_t message = kernel::R32(ctx.esp + 4);
    bool press = message == kMsgPadAccept || message == kMsgPadStart;
    if (!Opt().skip_movies || (!press && message != kMsgTick)) return;
    int& ticks = g_movie_ticks[ctx.ecx];
    if (press) {
        if (ticks > kSkipTick) kernel::W32(ctx.esp + 4, kMsgTick);  // ended already
        else if (!allow_flag || kernel::G<uint8_t>(ctx.ecx + allow_flag)) ticks = kSkipTick + 1;  // the player's ends it
        return;
    }
    if (ticks > kSkipTick || ++ticks < kSkipTick) return;
    if (allow_flag && !kernel::G<uint8_t>(ctx.ecx + allow_flag)) {
        ticks = kSkipTick - 1;  // not yet: the next tick asks again
        return;
    }
    ticks = kSkipTick + 1;
    kernel::W32(ctx.esp + 4, kMsgPadAccept);
}
void ForgetMovie(uint32_t screen) { g_movie_ticks.erase(screen); }

// only English and Indonesian are offered; Indonesian plays the English table, translated (prompts.cpp)
bool LanguageAvailable(const std::string& code) { return code == "int" || code == "ind"; }

// GameFlowManager's state (0x4936B8, written by 0x1C5CD7 and the rest): 3 the front end, 6 racing, loading between
constexpr uint32_t kGameFlowState = 0x4936B8;
constexpr uint32_t kGameFlowRacing = 6;
bool Racing() { return mem::IsCommitted(kGameFlowState) && kernel::R32(kGameFlowState) == kGameFlowRacing; }

}  // namespace game

// The drops on the screen in the rain (0x0CC530, a view's "Rain Drop" pass): 20 of them, each a copy of the frame into
// a 32x32 target and a draw back, 40 renderings a frame. SCREEN RAINDROPS off returns at once (cdecl, the view)
X86_EXTERN_FUNC(__imp__sub_000CC530);
X86_FUNC(sub_000CC530) {
    if (game::Opt().rain_drops) return __imp__sub_000CC530(ctx, base);
    ctx.esp += 4;
}

// The falling rain: a view's precipitation ([view + 0x68], 0x0D818A) draws its 350 drops (+0x33D8, the RAINDROP texture
// at +0x3404) in 0x2527A0. FALLING RAIN off returns at once (thiscall, nothing on the stack); the rain's strength
// (+0x290), which wets the road, is still worked out around it
X86_EXTERN_FUNC(__imp__sub_002527A0);

    if (game::Opt().rain) return __imp__sub_002527A0(ctx, base);

// The yellow look: the "Visual Look Pass" (0x0CDA40, pixel shader 0x17) adds the scene times a tint (texture 3) over
// the desaturated scene. 0x0C1BD0 fills that tint's 256x1 ramp ([this + 0x234]) from a curve (+0x50) times the colour
// at +0xA0/+0xA4/+0xA8 (R, G, B), the visual treatment's, blended by the game through the day. YELLOW TINT off makes
// the ramp grey of the colour's luma while it is built, and gives the game its colour back
X86_EXTERN_FUNC(__imp__sub_000C1BD0);
X86_FUNC(sub_000C1BD0) {
    if (game::Opt().yellow_tint) return __imp__sub_000C1BD0(ctx, base);
    uint32_t tint = ctx.ecx + 0xA0;
    float& r = kernel::G<float>(tint);
    float& g = kernel::G<float>(tint + 4);
    float& b = kernel::G<float>(tint + 8);
    float saved[] = {r, g, b};
    r = g = b = 0.299f * saved[0] + 0.587f * saved[1] + 0.114f * saved[2];
    __imp__sub_000C1BD0(ctx, base);
    r = saved[0], g = saved[1], b = saved[2];
}

// The motion blur: the "Motion Blur" pass (0x0D1440, cdecl: the view, a flag, a mode, an amount; from the "Visual Look
// Filters" at 0x0D2382) blends the frame with the ones before it by the car's speed, and returns whether it drew; the
// "Radial Blur Mask Pass" (0x0CE1C0, nitrous and the speedbreaker) follows only then. Slow, it draws nothing and
// returns false itself (0x0D1661): MOTION BLUR off returns so at once
X86_EXTERN_FUNC(__imp__sub_000D1440);
X86_FUNC(sub_000D1440) {
    if (game::Opt().motion_blur) return __imp__sub_000D1440(ctx, base);
    ctx.eax &= ~0xFFu;
    ctx.esp += 4;
}
```

`src/game/game_font.cpp`:

```cpp
// The game's body font (FONT_MW_BODY, the options' rows and most of the menus) for the ImGui panel. cFEng keeps its
// loaded fonts in a list at 0x48F2F0 (FindFont 0x137A40): a node's TextureInfo at +8, its FNTX resource at +0xC, its
// name's bStringHash at +0x14. The resource ('FNTX'): glyph count u16 +0xA, flags +0xC (0x40000: 16 byte glyphs),
// glyph table offset +0x14, line height +0x24. A glyph: Unicode u16 +0, width u8 +2, height u8 +3, its place in the
// texture u16 +4 / +6, x offset s8 +9, y offset from the line's top s8 +0xA, advance s16 +0xE (0x137EB0, 0x123620).
// The texture is 256x256 DXT3, linear (NV2A format 0x0E; the D3D texture at the TextureInfo's platform record +0x10).
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>

#include "common/game_font.h"
#include "core/log.h"
#include "kernel/kernel.h"
#include "kernel/memory.h"

namespace game {

namespace {

constexpr uint32_t kFontList = 0x48F2F0, kFontHash = 0x545570C6;  // bStringHash("FONT_MW_BODY")
constexpr uint32_t kFntx = 0x58544E46, kGlyphs16 = 0x40000, kFormatDxt3 = 0x0E;

std::mutex g_lock;
FontImage g_font;
bool g_ready = false, g_taken = false, g_tried = false;

bool Readable(uint32_t va, uint32_t n) { return va && mem::IsCommitted(va) && mem::IsCommitted(va + n - 1); }

// DXT3 to alpha alone: the glyphs are white, their alpha the explicit 4 bits a texel
std::vector<uint8_t> DecodeAlpha(const uint8_t* data, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {
    std::vector<uint8_t> out(size_t(w) * h);
    for (uint32_t by = 0; by < h / 4; by++)
        for (uint32_t bx = 0; bx < w / 4; bx++, data += 16) {
            uint64_t alpha;
            std::memcpy(&alpha, data, 8);
            for (uint32_t k = 0; k < 16; k++)
                out[size_t(by * 4 + k / 4) * w + bx * 4 + k % 4] = uint8_t(((alpha >> (4 * k)) & 15) * 17);
        }
    return out;
}

}  // namespace

void CaptureFont() {
    if (g_tried || !Readable(kFontList, 4)) return;
    uint32_t node = kernel::R32(kFontList);
    for (int k = 0; node && node != kFontList && k < 64; node = kernel::R32(node), k++)
        if (Readable(node, 0x18) && kernel::R32(node + 0x14) == kFontHash) break;
    if (!node || node == kFontList || !Readable(node, 0x18)) return;  // not loaded yet
    g_tried = true;
    uint32_t res = kernel::R32(node + 0xC), info = kernel::R32(node + 8);
    if (!Readable(res, 0x28) || kernel::R32(res) != kFntx || !(kernel::R32(res + 0xC) & kGlyphs16) ||
        !Readable(info, 4)) {
        LOGW("font: FONT_MW_BODY is not a font this reads");
        return;
    }
    uint32_t plat = kernel::R32(info), d3d = plat + 0x10;
    if (!Readable(plat, 0x20)) return;
    uint32_t format = kernel::R32(d3d + 12);
    uint32_t w = 1u << ((format >> 20) & 15), h = 1u << ((format >> 24) & 15);
    uint32_t data = mem::VirtualFromPhysical(kernel::R32(d3d + 4));
    if (((format >> 8) & 0xFF) != kFormatDxt3 || w < 4 || h < 4 || !Readable(data, w * h)) {
        LOGW("font: FONT_MW_BODY's texture is format %08X, not DXT3", format);
        return;
    }
    std::vector<uint8_t> alpha = DecodeAlpha(static_cast<const uint8_t*>(kernel::HostPtr(data)), w, h);
    FontImage font;
    font.line_height = int(kernel::R32(res + 0x24));
    uint32_t count = kernel::R32(res + 8) >> 16, table = res + kernel::R32(res + 0x14);
    if (!Readable(table, count * 16)) return;
    const uint8_t* g = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(kernel::HostPtr(table));
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++, g += 16) {
        FontGlyph glyph;
        uint16_t code, x, y;
        int16_t advance;
        std::memcpy(&code, g, 2);
        std::memcpy(&x, g + 4, 2);
        std::memcpy(&y, g + 6, 2);
        std::memcpy(&advance, g + 0xE, 2);
        glyph.code = code;
        glyph.w = g[2];
        glyph.h = g[3];
        glyph.x_off = int8_t(g[9]);
        glyph.y_off = int8_t(g[0xA]);
        glyph.advance = advance;
        if (x + uint32_t(glyph.w) > w || y + uint32_t(glyph.h) > h) continue;
        glyph.alpha.resize(size_t(glyph.w) * glyph.h);
        for (int row = 0; row < glyph.h; row++)
            std::memcpy(glyph.alpha.data() + size_t(row) * glyph.w, alpha.data() + size_t(y + row) * w + x, size_t(glyph.w));
        font.glyphs.push_back(std::move(glyph));
    }
    LOGI("font: FONT_MW_BODY, %zu glyphs, %d high", font.glyphs.size(), font.line_height);
    std::lock_guard guard(g_lock);
    g_font = std::move(font);
    g_ready = true;
}

bool TakeFont(FontImage& out) {
    std::lock_guard guard(g_lock);
    if (!g_ready || g_taken) return false;
    g_taken = true;
    out = std::move(g_font);
    return true;
}

}  // namespace game
```
